mainTopic: Conditional גיטין: אביי's two-condition reading, 'your presence,' גט ישן, the משנה of 'מעכשיו' and the husband's death, and רבותינו's lenient ruling.
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing the משנה's travel cases. Twice, a husband who turned back at אנטיפרס or at עכו seems to clash with the geography, and both times אביי answers that the husband set two conditions: reaching the destination, or thirty days on the road. Next comes the husband who said 'if I pass from your presence thirty days' and kept coming and going. רב הונא says 'your presence' means marital relations. רבי יוחנן says it is literal, and that the גט simply has not become a גט ישן. A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן. The worry that he won her over is answered by a husband who said she is believed to say he did not come, and the גמרא brings two versions of where this answer was said. A new משנה then teaches that without 'מעכשיו' a husband's death within twelve months cancels the גט, while with it the גט is valid. The same משנה covers instructions to messengers to 'write and give,' where רבי יוסי disagrees, and a case where it is unknown whether the גט or the death came first. The גמרא reports that 'our Rabbis' (the court of רבי יהודה נשיאה) let her remarry, following רבי יוסי's rule that a document's date shows when it takes effect. It then discusses רבי אלעזר's question of when she was freed. At the end, אביי begins a statement about a גט tied to sunrise, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The end of the challenge about אנטיפרס
steps.stepSummary: These are the closing words of a challenge from the previous section. That challenge quoted a source that ends in doubt about whether the woman is divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...or whether she is not divorced!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge it began just before this point. The challenge questions how the משנה understands where אנטיפרס is located.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source being quoted leaves the woman in doubt, divorced or not divorced. That seems to clash with how the משנה treats the trip to אנטיפרס. This clash sets up אביי's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: divorced (a woman whose גט has taken effect)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this line as a ruling of its own. It is only the tail end of a quote that belongs to the challenge before it.

phrases.english: ...or she is not divorced!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of the husband who went toward the גליל and turned back at אנטיפרס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source about this geography leaves the divorce in doubt, which seems to contradict the משנה's assumption about where אנטיפרס is.

steps.title: Two conditions: reaching the גליל or thirty days on the road
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the husband made two separate conditions. Turning back at אנטיפרס fulfills neither one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He set two conditions for her. 'If I reach the גליל, let it be a גט right away. And if I am delayed on the road thirty days and don't come back, let it be a גט.' If he reached אנטיפרס and came back, he neither reached the גליל nor was delayed thirty days, so his condition is void.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by rereading what the husband meant. The husband had two separate triggers for the גט in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the משנה treats reaching אנטיפרס as reaching the גליל. אביי says the משנה treats אנטיפרס as a stop still short of the גליל: the גט takes effect only once he actually reaches the גליל or is delayed thirty days. Coming back early from אנטיפרס meets neither trigger, so nothing happens.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a single sentence in a גט condition can contain more than one trigger. The גמרא will use this same tool again right away for עכו.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
He was saying two conditions to her:
If I reach the Galilee,
let it be a bill of divorce immediately;
and if I am delayed on the way thirty days
and do not come back, let it be a bill of divorce.
If he reached Antipatris and returned,
since he did not reach the Galilee,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אִישְׁתַּהוֹיֵי נָמֵי אִשְׁתַּהִי תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין –
phrases.english: and he also was not delayed thirty days,
his condition is void.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, תְּרֵי תְּנָאֵי קָאָמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about אנטיפרס.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the husband's words as two separate conditions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case depends on whether אנטיפרס is inside or outside the גליל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גט depends on actually reaching the גליל or being delayed thirty days, and neither happened.

steps.title: Is עכו really outside ארץ ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, which treats a man who turns back at עכו as not having gone overseas. It then challenges this from רב ספרא, who shows that עכו is inside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'This is your גט if I do not come back within thirty days,' etc. Does this mean עכו counts as overseas? But רב ספרא said: when the רבנן took leave of each other, they parted at עכו, because it is forbidden to leave ארץ ישראל for חוץ לארץ!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, the man traveling overseas who turned back at עכו. It raises a geography problem with this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to treat reaching עכו as reaching overseas. But רב ספרא's report shows that עכו was the last stop still inside ארץ ישראל: the friends escorting a traveler went only as far as עכו, since going farther would mean leaving ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: a country overseas, outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: "This is your bill of divorce

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא בָּאתִי מִכָּאן וְעַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם״ כּוּ׳:
phrases.english: if I do not come from now until thirty days," etc.
Is this to say that Akko is located overseas?!
But didn't Rav Safra say:
When the Rabbis would take leave of one another,
they would take leave in Akko,
phrases.notes: They escorted the traveler only as far as עכו, the last spot still inside the Land.

phrases.english: because it is forbidden to go out
from the Land to outside the Land!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה and raises a parallel geography problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of the man going overseas who turned back at עכו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב ספרא's report proves עכו is inside ארץ ישראל, so the משנה cannot be treating it as overseas.

steps.title: The same two-condition answer for עכו
steps.stepSummary: אביי applies the same two-condition reading to the overseas case. Turning back at עכו fulfills neither condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He set two conditions. 'If I reach overseas, let it be a גט right away. If I am delayed on the road thirty days and don't come back, let it be a גט.' If he reached עכו and came back, he neither reached overseas nor was delayed thirty days, so his condition is void.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the עכו challenge with exactly the same approach he used for אנטיפרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה never claimed that עכו is overseas. עכו is simply where he turned back, before reaching his overseas destination. Since he also returned before thirty days had passed, neither trigger for the גט happened.
steps.whatToRemember: In both the אנטיפרס case and the עכו case, אביי reads the husband's words as two separate conditions: reaching the destination makes the גט take effect immediately, and being delayed thirty days on the road also makes it take effect. Turning back early meets neither condition, so the condition is void and she is not divorced.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
He was saying two conditions to her:
If I reach a country overseas,
let it be a bill of divorce immediately;
if I am delayed on the way thirty days
and do not come back, let it be a bill of divorce.
If he reached Akko and returned,
since he did not reach a country overseas,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אִישְׁתַּהוֹיֵי נָמֵי אִשְׁתַּהִי תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין –
phrases.english: and he also was not delayed thirty days,
his condition is void.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, תְּרֵי תְּנָאֵי קָאָמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the עכו challenge using the same method as step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the husband's words as two separate conditions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה treats reaching עכו as reaching overseas.
steps.terutzMaskana: עכו is just where he turned back. The גט required actually reaching overseas or being delayed thirty days, and neither happened.

steps.title: How can it be a valid divorce if he never stayed away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and asks how the גט works, since the husband kept coming back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'This is your גט if at any time I pass away from you for thirty days,' and so on. But he did not pass away from her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה about a husband who kept coming and going. It asks a question: he never actually stayed away, so why is it a valid גט?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition was that he stay away from her for thirty days. Because he kept coming and going, it looks like the condition never happened. A גט whose condition was never met should not work.

keyTerms.meaning: that I will pass away (from you)
but he did not pass away!
etc.: the quote of the משנה continues

phrases.aramaic: ״הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁאֶעֱבוֹר״ וְכוּ׳:
phrases.english: "This is your bill of divorce if at any time I pass away" etc.:
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה says 'from your presence for thirty days.' He kept going and coming, and the משנה still calls it a valid גט.

phrases.english: But he did not pass away from her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the same משנה after the עכו discussion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the גט is valid even though he kept coming and going.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The condition (staying away thirty days) was never met, so the גט should not work.

steps.title: רב הונא: 'Your face' means marital relations
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that 'your face' is a polite way of saying marital relations, and that condition was met.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: What does 'your face' mean? Marital relations. And why does he call it 'your face'? He used a polite expression.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question by changing what the condition means. 'Passing away from your face' really means not being intimate with her for thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the condition is about intimacy and not about being nearby, then coming and going does not matter. He was never intimate with her during the thirty days, so the condition was met and the גט works.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
What is 'your face'? Marital relations;
and why does he call it 'your face'?
He used a refined expression.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Your face' means being physically near her, so coming and going breaks the condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Your face' means intimacy, which did not happen, so the condition was met.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'Your face' is literal, and the גט will work later
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן keeps the plain meaning and rereads the משנה: the גט has not become old and will take effect once thirty days away are completed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Really, 'your face' means literally your face. Does the משנה say 'she is divorced'? It says 'this is a גט.' That means it does not become a גט ישן, and when thirty days are completed later, it will be a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer. He keeps 'your face' as meaning his actual presence, and he rereads what the משנה is ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה never says she is divorced now. It only says the document is still a usable גט. Since he was never alone with her, it has not turned into a 'גט ישן.' Whenever he later stays away a full thirty days, the divorce takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: an 'old' גט: one after which the husband was alone with his wife, which the חכמים said should not be used

steps.confusionAlert: 'הרי זה גט' (this is a גט) is not the same as 'הרי זו מגורשת' (she is divorced). For רבי יוחנן, the משנה only says the paper is still good. She is not divorced yet.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Really, 'your face' means literally your face.
Does it teach 'she is divorced'?
It teaches 'this is a bill of divorce':
meaning it does not become an old bill of divorce,
phrases.notes: Since he was never alone with her, the paper has not gone 'stale.'

phrases.aramaic: וּלְכִי מָלוּ תְּלָתִין יוֹמֵי הָוֵי גִּיטָּא.
phrases.english: and when thirty days are completed, it becomes a bill of divorce.
phrases.notes: He means thirty days in a row that he really stays away, whenever that happens later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא and answers step 5's question another way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading what the משנה's ruling means
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'הרי זה גט' means she is divorced right now.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only means the גט is not old and will work once the condition is truly met.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that the גט is valid and not a גט ישן because he was never alone with her, which fits רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן: 'This is your גט if at any time I pass away from before your face thirty days,' and he kept coming and going. Since he was not alone with her, this is a גט. And we are not worried about a גט ישן, since he was not alone with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's whole concern is whether the גט became a גט ישן, and it answers that it did not, because he was never alone with her. That is exactly רבי יוחנן's reading of 'this is a גט.' Under רב הונא, there would be no need to talk about a גט ישן at all.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא was taught that agrees with him

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא backs רבי יוחנן: 'your face' means his actual presence, and the גט stays usable because he was never alone with her.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan:
"This is your bill of divorce if at any time
I pass away from before your face for thirty days,"
and he kept going and coming, going and coming;

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְלֹא נִתְיַיחֵד עִמָּהּ – הֲרֵי זֶה גֵּט;
phrases.english: since he was not secluded with her, this is a bill of divorce;
and we are not concerned about an old bill of divorce,
since he was not secluded with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבי יוחנן's answer in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's reading: the גט is not old and stays usable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא) that speaks of 'מנגד פניך' and rules there is no concern of גט ישן.

steps.title: Maybe he won her over and was alone with her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: since he kept coming, maybe he won her over and was alone with her, making the גט old.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us be concerned that perhaps he won her over!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's claim that he was not alone with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא relies on the fact that he was never alone with her. But he kept coming back, so maybe he won her over and they were alone together. Then the גט would be a גט ישן after all.

phrases.english: But let us be concerned that perhaps he won her over!
phrases.notes: He means: won her over and was alone with her during one of his visits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא brought in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that he was not secluded with her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His repeated visits make seclusion possible, so how can we be sure the גט is not old?

steps.title: The husband said he trusts her to say he did not come
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא, quoting רב, explains that the case is where the husband said she is believed to say he did not come.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: So said my father, my teacher, in the name of רב: The case is where the husband says, 'She is believed by me to say that I did not come.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the worry of step 9 by narrowing the case of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband made her trustworthy about whether he came to her. So if she says he was not alone with her, we accept it, and the worry that he won her over goes away. The גט stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: she is believed by me (I trust her word)
that I did not come (to her)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא works because the husband himself gave her the power to say he did not come, so we do not worry that he won her over.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר אַבָּא מָרִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב,
phrases.english: So said my father, my teacher, in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: בְּאוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמֶנֶת עָלַי לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא בָּאתִי.
phrases.english: It is where he says: She is believed by me to say that I did not come.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמֶנֶת עָלַי לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא בָּאתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry raised in step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We cannot know whether he was alone with her, so the גט might be old.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband made her believed, so her word that he did not come settles it.

steps.title: A second version: the teaching was said on a later משנה
steps.stepSummary: Some place רב's teaching on a משנה where the husband said 'from now, if I do not come within twelve months' and then died. That משנה rules the גט is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people teach this on the משנה: 'From now, if I do not come back within twelve months,' and he died within the twelve months, the גט is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of where the earlier discussion took place. This step sets up a question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the question and רב's answer were about the ברייתא of the husband who kept coming and going. This version moves the whole discussion onto a משנה found later. In that case the husband said 'from now', so the גט takes effect from the day it was given, and his death does not cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (another version of where a statement was said)
From now (the גט takes effect from the day it is given)

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה quoted here is not the one that just appeared before. It is a later case that includes the word 'מעכשיו', and that word is what makes the גט valid.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on the Mishnah:
phrases.notes: The 'it' is רב's teaching from the step before: 'she is believed to say I did not come.'

phrases.english: "From now, if I do not come back
from now until twelve months,"
and he died within twelve months,
it is a valid bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of where the question and answer of steps 9 and 10 were said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט given 'from now, if I do not come within twelve months' is valid even if the husband dies within the twelve months.

steps.title: Maybe he made up with her during the year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: we should worry that he won her over and was alone with her before he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we should worry that maybe he made up with her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that the גט is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband was alone with his wife after giving the גט, there is a problem of a גט ישן (an 'old' גט). This version asks the same question as step 9, but now it is aimed at the משנה instead of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: He won her over / made up with her (and was alone with her)

phrases.english: But let us be concerned that perhaps he won her over!
phrases.notes: He means: maybe he came back quietly, made up with her, and was alone with her before he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the משנה quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the 'from now' גט is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There may have been private reconciliation and being alone together before he died, which would make it a גט ישן.

steps.title: He said she is believed to say he did not come
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא, quoting his father in the name of רב, answers that the case is where the husband said she is believed to say he did not come.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: This is what my father, my teacher, said in the name of רב: The case is where the husband said, 'She is believed by me to say that I did not come.'
steps.whatsHappening: The same answer from step 10 is given again, now to protect the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband gave his wife full credibility, so if she says he never came back, we accept it. There is then no worry that they were alone together. The words are repeated because in this version they answer a question about the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: My father, my teacher (here, רב הונא)

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר אַבָּא מָרִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב,
phrases.english: So said my father, my teacher, in the name of Rav:
Where he says: She is believed by me
to say that I did not come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא הָכִי אָמַר אַבָּא מָרִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about any husband who said 'from now', so we must worry he was alone with her.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a husband who made his wife believed to say he did not come, so there is no worry.

steps.title: Comparing the two versions
steps.stepSummary: If רב's teaching was said on the משנה, it surely applies to the ברייתא too. If it was said on the ברייתא, the משנה does not need it, because there the husband never came back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever teaches it on the משנה would surely apply it to the ברייתא. But whoever teaches it on the ברייתא would say that in the משנה there is no need for it, because the husband never came back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the two versions differ in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא the husband kept coming and going, so the worry that they were alone together is strong. In the משנה he never came back and then died, so the worry is weak. If the weak case needs רב's condition, the strong case surely does, but the reverse is not true.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that is outside the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Version 1 (on the ברייתא): only the coming-and-going case needs 'she is believed'. Version 2 (on the משנה): both cases need it.

phrases.english: The one who teaches it on the Mishnah
all the more so on the baraita.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is the case from step 8, where the husband kept coming and going.

phrases.english: The one who teaches it on the baraita,
but on the Mishnah, he did not come.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַמַּתְנִיתִין כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אַבָּרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out what each version means in practice, comparing step 10 with step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה version makes the condition needed in both cases. The ברייתא version makes it needed only where the husband kept visiting.

steps.title: New משנה: without 'from now', death cancels the divorce
steps.stepSummary: If the husband said 'this is your גט if I do not come within twelve months' without saying 'from now', and he died within the twelve months, the גט is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If he said, 'This is your גט if I do not come back within twelve months,' and he died within twelve months, it is not a valid גט.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a case close to the one before, but this time the husband did not say 'from now'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'from now', the גט would only take effect at the end of the twelve months. By that time the husband is already dead, and a גט cannot take effect after the husband's death.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a valid bill of divorce

steps.confusionAlert: The two cases differ by only one word. With 'מעכשיו' the גט is valid (step 11). Without it the גט is not valid (here).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the words 'from now' decide whether a conditional גט still works when the husband dies.

phrases.english: MISHNA: "This is your bill of divorce

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא בָּאתִי מִכָּאן וְעַד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ״,
phrases.english: if I do not come back from now until twelve months,"
phrases.notes: Notice that the word 'מעכשיו' (from now) is missing here, unlike the case in step 11.

phrases.english: and he died within twelve months,
it is not a valid bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּךְ אִם לֹא בָּאתִי מִכָּאן וְעַד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה that is a contrast case to the 'from now' case quoted in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A conditional גט without 'from now' is not valid if the husband dies before the condition is fulfilled.

steps.title: Saying 'from now' makes the גט valid even if he dies within the year
steps.stepSummary: If the husband said 'this is your גט from now, if I do not come within twelve months' and died within the twelve months, the גט is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'This is your גט from now, if I do not come back within twelve months,' and he died within the twelve months, it is a valid גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case to the last step. This time the husband added the word 'from now', and here the גט works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 there was no 'from now', so the גט could only take effect after the twelve months, and by then he was already dead. Here 'from now' means that once the condition comes true, the גט counts from the moment it was handed over, while he was still alive. He never came back, so the condition came true and the גט is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: from now, so the גט takes effect from the time it was given
if I do not come back, which is the condition

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 15. There the wording is the same except for 'from now', and the ruling is the opposite. That one word changes everything.

phrases.english: "This is your bill of divorce from now,
if I do not come back from now
until twelve months"
and he died within twelve months,
this is a valid bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasting case to step 15: the same wording with 'from now' added
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With 'from now', the גט takes effect from the time it was given, so his death within the twelve months does not cancel it.

steps.title: Condition said first, then 'write and give': writing it early cancels the גט
steps.stepSummary: The husband said 'if I do not come within twelve months, write and give a גט to my wife.' They wrote it during the twelve months and gave it after, so it is not a valid גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'If I do not come back within twelve months, write and give a גט to my wife,' and they wrote it during the twelve months and gave it after the twelve months, it is not a valid גט.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the husband is not handing over a גט himself. He is instructing others to write one and give it. The משנה rules that they wrote it too soon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He put the condition before both instructions, so permission to write only begins once the twelve months are over. A גט written before he gave permission to write it is not valid, even though it was handed over at the right time.

keyTerms.meaning: write and give, the husband's instruction to the messengers
it is not a valid גט

phrases.english: "If I do not come back from now
until twelve months,
write and give a bill of divorce to my wife"

phrases.aramaic: כָּתְבוּ גֵּט בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: and they wrote a bill of divorce within twelve months,
and gave it after twelve months,
it is not a valid bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם לֹא בָּאתִי מִכָּאן וְעַד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ, כִּתְבוּ וּתְנוּ גֵּט לְאִשְׁתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New case in the same משנה: a גט made through messengers instead of handed over by the husband
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the condition comes before 'write and give', the writing also has to wait until after the twelve months. Writing it early makes the גט invalid.

steps.title: 'Write and give' said first, then the condition: still invalid according to the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: With the order reversed ('write and give… if I do not come'), writing during the year and giving after it is still not a valid גט according to the first opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'Write and give a גט to my wife if I do not come back within twelve months,' and they wrote it during the twelve months and gave it after, it is not a valid גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the last case with the words in a different order. The first opinion gives the same ruling: not valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though 'write and give' comes first, the תנא קמא understands that the condition at the end still applies to the writing as well as the giving. So writing it early is still writing without permission. This step sets up רבי יוסי's disagreement in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: "Write and give a bill of divorce to my wife,

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא בָּאתִי מִכָּאן עַד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ״ –
phrases.english: if I do not come back from now until twelve months"
and they wrote it within twelve months,
and gave it after twelve months,
it is not a valid bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּתְבוּ וּתְנוּ גֵּט לְאִשְׁתִּי, אִם לֹא בָּאתִי מִכָּאן עַד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same case as step 17 with the order of the words reversed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, the condition still covers the writing, so a גט written within the twelve months is invalid.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: with this word order the גט is valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rules that in this version of the wording, the גט is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: in a case like this, it is a valid גט.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the תנא קמא about the reversed word order only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the husband said 'write' before he mentioned any condition, רבי יוסי reads the condition as applying only to the giving. So the messengers were allowed to write it at any time. What mattered was that they gave it after the twelve months, and they did.

keyTerms.meaning: like this, meaning in this word order

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is only talking about the second wording, where 'write and give' comes first. He agrees with step 17, where the condition came first.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
In a case like this, it is a valid bill of divorce.
phrases.notes: 'Like this' points to the wording he just heard, where 'write and give' came before the condition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's ruling in step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When 'write and give' comes before the condition, the condition applies only to the giving, so writing early is allowed and the גט is valid.

steps.title: Written and given at the right time, but the husband died: which came first?
steps.stepSummary: If they wrote and gave the גט after twelve months and the husband died, the גט is valid if it was given before the death and invalid if the death came first. If nobody knows, she is in doubt: 'divorced and not divorced.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If they wrote it after twelve months and gave it after twelve months, and the husband died: if the גט came before the death, it is valid. If the death came before the גט, it is not valid. If nobody knows, this is the case the חכמים meant when they said 'she is divorced and not divorced.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with the case where the messengers did everything correctly, but the husband died around the same time. The ruling depends on the timing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט cannot take effect after the husband has died, so it only works if it reached her while he was still alive. When the order is unknown, she is treated as in doubt and gets the strict rules of both a divorced woman and a married one.

keyTerms.meaning: divorced and not divorced, a state of doubt

steps.whatToRemember: Three things decide these cases: whether he said 'from now', what the condition covers (writing, giving, or both), and whether the גט reached her before he died. If the timing is unknown, she is in doubt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule that a גט needs a living husband at the moment it is given. It also shows how a doubt about timing leaves the woman in an in-between status.

phrases.english: If they wrote it after twelve months,

phrases.aramaic: וְנָתְנוּ לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ, וָמֵת;
phrases.english: and gave it after twelve months, and he died;

phrases.aramaic: אִם הַגֵּט קוֹדֵם לַמִּיתָה – הֲרֵי זֶה גֵּט;
phrases.english: if the bill of divorce came before the death, it is a valid bill of divorce;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם מִיתָה קָדְמָה לַגֵּט – אֵינוֹ גֵּט;
phrases.english: and if the death came before the bill of divorce, it is not a valid bill of divorce;
and if it is not known which came first,
this is the case of which they said:
she is divorced and not divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתְבוּ לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ, וְנָתְנוּ לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ, וָמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final case of the משנה: the messengers acted correctly, but the husband's death raises a question of timing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט given before the husband's death is valid. One given after his death is not. If the order is unknown, she is in doubt: divorced and not divorced.

steps.title: A ברייתא: our Rabbis permitted her to remarry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying that 'our Rabbis' allowed the woman to remarry, even though the משנה said the גט is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught in a ברייתא: Our Rabbis permitted her to marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by quoting a ברייתא that disagrees with it: 'our Rabbis' allowed the woman to remarry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that if the husband died within the twelve months, the גט is not valid. These Rabbis treat the גט as valid, so the woman is free to marry anyone. That sets up the next question: who are these Rabbis, and what is their reasoning?

keyTerms.meaning: Our Rabbis: a special group of later חכמים

steps.confusionAlert: This is about the case where the husband did NOT say 'from now.' In the 'from now' case (Step 16), everyone already agrees the גט is valid.

phrases.english: Gemara:
It was taught: Our Rabbis permitted her to marry.
phrases.notes: This is going back to the משנה's case where he died inside the twelve months and the משנה said 'not a גט.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה by quoting a ברייתא that rules against the משנה's 'not a גט' ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to 'our Rabbis,' the woman whose husband died within the twelve months may remarry.

steps.title: Who are 'our Rabbis'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the 'Rabbis' in the ברייתא are.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are 'our Rabbis'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple identification question. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Our Rabbis' is an unusual title, so the גמרא wants to know exactly which group of חכמים this refers to.

phrases.english: Who are 'our Rabbis'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the group named in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the 'Rabbis' who permitted the woman to remarry.

steps.title: The court that permitted oil, following רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says they are the court that permitted non-Jewish oil. They hold like רבי יוסי: the date written on a document shows that it takes effect from that date.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: It is the court that permitted oil. They hold like רבי יוסי, who says: The date written on a document proves when it takes effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. It names the court and explains why that court thinks the גט is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every גט has a date written on it. According to רבי יוסי, that date shows the husband wanted it to take effect from the day it was written, as if he had said 'from now.' So even though he died before the year was over, the גט already started working back on the date, before his death.

keyTerms.meaning: The date written on a document
Proves about it (shows when it takes effect)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how 'our Rabbis' could disagree with the משנה: the written date counts as if the husband had said 'from now.'

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
It is the court that permitted oil;
phrases.notes: This means oil made by non-Jews, which had been forbidden until this court permitted it.

phrases.english: they hold like Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: זְמַנּוֹ שֶׁל שְׁטָר מוֹכִיחַ עָלָיו.
phrases.english: who says: The date of a document proves about it.
phrases.notes: Since the גט is dated, it counts as if he said 'from now,' even though he never said those words.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בֵּי דִינָא דִּשְׁרוֹ מִישְׁחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the identification question and adds the reasoning behind the ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Our Rabbis' are the court that permitted oil, and they follow רבי יוסי's rule that a document's date shows it takes effect from that date.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה ruled this, but his colleagues did not agree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that רבי יהודה נשיאה gave this ruling, and his colleagues did not agree with him. Another version says they did not agree with him for his whole life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא son of רבי חייא בר אבא said that רבי יוחנן said: רבי יהודה נשיאה, son of רבן גמליאל son of רבי, taught this ruling, and his whole group did not agree with him. Some say: his whole lifetime.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a report about who gave this lenient ruling and how the other חכמים reacted to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is credited to רבי יהודה נשיאה, but it was not accepted. The two versions differ only in wording: either his colleagues did not agree with him (סיעתו), or nobody agreed with him during his lifetime (שעתו).

keyTerms.meaning: They did not agree with him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba, said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Rabbi Yehuda Nesia,

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בַּר רַבִּי הוֹרָה,
phrases.english: son of Rabban Gamliel son of Rabbi, ruled this,
phrases.notes: 'רבי' here is רבי יהודה הנשיא, so רבי יהודה נשיאה is his grandson.

phrases.english: and his whole group did not agree with him;
and some say: his whole lifetime.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a report that names who gave the lenient ruling and notes that it was not accepted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה נשיאה permitted her to remarry, but his colleagues did not agree with him.

steps.title: Did they let her remarry right away or after twelve months?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks an elder from that court whether they let the woman remarry right after the husband died, or only after the twelve months were over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said to a certain elder: When you permitted her, did you permit her right away, or after twelve months? Right away, since he is certainly not coming? Or perhaps after twelve months, since only then was his condition fulfilled?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks a practical question about the lenient ruling: from what point was the woman allowed to remarry?
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side: once the husband is dead, he obviously will never come back, so the condition is as good as fulfilled right away. The other side: the condition was 'if I do not come within twelve months,' so technically it is only fulfilled when the twelve months are over.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְהָהוּא סָבָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said to a certain elder:
When you permitted her, did you permit her immediately,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ שְׁרִיתוּהָ?
phrases.english: or did you permit her after twelve months?
Did you permit her immediately, because he is certainly not coming?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ שְׁרִיתוּהָ –
phrases.english: Or perhaps you permitted her after twelve months,
because only then was his condition fulfilled?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְהָהוּא סָבָא: כִּי שְׁרִיתוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who gave the ruling to exactly how it was applied in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the woman may remarry immediately after the husband's death, since he will certainly not come back, or only after the twelve months, when the condition is technically fulfilled.

steps.title: The same question could be asked about the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי אלעזר's question also applies to the משנה's case of 'from now, if I do not come back within twelve months,' where the husband died inside the twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him ask this question about our משנה too. The husband said, 'This is your גט from now, if I do not come back from now until twelve months,' and he died within the twelve months, and the משנה says it is a valid גט. Does the גט work right away when he dies, since he certainly will not come back? Or does it only work after the twelve months are over, since only then is his condition fully met?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר needed to ask an elder from that court. The very same question could be asked about a case already in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's 'from now' case the גט is valid, but it is not clear when the woman is free. Once he dies, we know he will never come back, so maybe she is free immediately. Or maybe the condition 'if I do not come within twelve months' is only fully met when the twelve months end. That is exactly the doubt רבי אלעזר raised about the court's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: From now. The גט takes effect from this moment if the condition is later met.
Or perhaps. This introduces the second side of a question.

phrases.english: But let him ask this question about our Mishnah:
'From now, if I do not come back
from now until twelve months,'
and he died within the twelve months:
this is a valid bill of divorce.
Is it a גט right away, since he certainly will not come back?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ –
phrases.english: Or perhaps it is a גט only after twelve months,
since only then is his condition fulfilled?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges why רבי אלעזר took his question in Step 25 to an elder, when the same doubt already comes up in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's choice to ask the elder from the court
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The question of 'immediately or after twelve months' exists equally in the משנה's מעכשיו case, so he could have asked it there without going to the court's elder

steps.title: Yes, but the elder had been there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the question applies to the משנה too. רבי אלעזר asked the elder because he had been present at the real incident.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. He asked the elder because the elder was there when that incident took place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It admits the question could be asked about the משנה, but explains that asking someone who saw the actual case is the best way to find out what was done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not say the משנה is different. It accepts that the same doubt exists there. The reason for going to the elder is practical: he was present at the event, so he could report what the court actually ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so. The גמרא is agreeing with the point just raised.
An actual incident or real case

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so;
and he asked him because he was present at that incident.
phrases.notes: 'He' here is the elder from the court that רבי אלעזר asked in Step 25.

steps.whatToRemember: The question 'free right away, or only after twelve months?' applies both to the court's ruling and to the משנה's 'from now' case. רבי אלעזר went to the elder only because the elder had seen the real case.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 26
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Asking the elder was unnecessary, since the same question exists in the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: The question does apply to the משנה, but the elder was an eyewitness to the actual ruling, so asking him made sense

steps.title: אביי begins: what everyone agrees on about 'when the sun comes out'
steps.stepSummary: אביי opens a new statement about a case everyone agrees on: a husband says the גט takes effect 'when the sun comes out of its sheath.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Everyone agrees that in a case where the husband said, 'When the sun comes out of its sheath'...
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. The גמרא is setting up אביי's statement, and his actual ruling continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'everyone agrees' tells us אביי is about to name a case where the opinions that usually argue would hold the same view. Here the husband ties the גט to something that is certain to happen: the sun rising. What the agreement is comes in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: A sheath or case. Here it is a picture of the sun rising out of its covering.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Everyone agrees
in a case where he said:
'When the sun comes out of its sheath'

steps.confusionAlert: אביי's sentence stops in the middle here. Don't try to work out the ruling yet; it comes in the next part.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section after the discussion of the elder's report is finished
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי sets up a case everyone agrees on, where the גט is tied to sunrise. His ruling continues on the next עמוד.
